**STEP 1 - Scene:** A snack of whole almonds in a white foam bowl, photographed from above on a wooden board.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A white foam cereal bowl, about 15 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 7.5² ≈ 177 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole almonds only. No oil, dressing, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The almonds fill the central part of the bowl and cover about 60% of the vessel area (≈106 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about 1.5 cm high. 106 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 160 ml gross.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole almonds have a bulk density nearer 0.5 g/ml than the listed nut-like densities, so I use 0.5. 160 ml × 0.5 ≈ 80 g. Counting the visible almonds (roughly 50 at about 1.2 g each) gives about 60 g. I take a midpoint of about 70 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Almonds are about 579 kcal per 100 g (raw/dry-roasted basis). 70 g × 5.79 ≈ 405 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 50 almonds in a small bowl is about 60–80 g, which is plausible. Total is roughly 70 g and 400 kcal.
